extra.message: Stored/DOM-based XSS in websocketMessageArrived(): attacker-controlled chatMessage.message and chatMessage.author.name (delivered over the Stomp websocket subscription at line 36 and originating from any user's unsanitized chat input via sendChatToBackend) are concatenated into an HTML string assigned to p.innerHTML and appended to the chat panel. A malicious user can send a message such as which executes in every recipient's session, enabling theft of the logged-in user data stored in localStorage.

extra.message: Stored XSS in showContactDetails(): buttonClicked.replaceWith(user.emailAddress) passes a user-controlled string to jQuery's replaceWith(), which parses HTML. user.emailAddress is set by any user at registration (Register.js) with no sanitization, so registering with an email such as causes script execution when another user clicks 'Click to show contact'.

extra.message: Stored XSS / arbitrary code execution via javascript: URL. renderUserProfile() places the fully attacker-controlled user.webPageUrl (freely set during registration, Register.js line 70) directly into the href attribute of an anchor without scheme validation. A registered attacker can set webPageUrl to 'javascript:...' so that when any victim views their profile and clicks 'Go to ...s web page', the script runs in the victim's origin/session.

extra.message: Reverse tabnabbing: the profile link uses target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer". The destination page (user.webPageUrl is attacker-controlled) can access window.opener and rewrite the parent app page (e.g. swap in a phishing login form), because the child tab retains a reference to the opener. Add rel="noopener noreferrer".

cwe: CWE-1022: Use of Web Link to Untrusted Target with window.opener Access

extra.message: Missing/hardcoded authentication for the websocket channel: every client connects to the STOMP endpoint with the same fixed credentials client.connect('asdf', 'were', ...) and subscribes to '/user/queue/notifications'. Because all users share one principal, the server cannot distinguish users, so notifications/chat intended for one user can be delivered to any client (cross-user data exposure / access-control bypass), and the channel provides no real authentication. This is the websocket authentication vulnerability described in the README.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: CSRF: session state is managed by cookies (all requests use credentials:'include' after cookie-based login) yet no CSRF token or origin check exists anywhere in the app. logoutClicked() performs a state-changing server call using a GET request, which any third-party page can trigger cross-origin via an /

Cleartext transmission of sensitive data: the backend base URLs use plain http:// (not https://). Login credentials (Login.js postLogin sends username/password to backendUrlBase+'login') and registration data including the password (Register.js:24-31) are transmitted unencrypted over the network, exposing them to eavesdropping/MITM. The backend IP is also hardcoded.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: Attacker-controlled user.name is concatenated unencoded into the URL query string (messages/chat?otherUser=' + user.name). A registered username containing URL metacharacters (&, =, #) can alter the request parameters sent to the backend, leading to request-parameter injection/poisoning that may let a user retrieve another user's chat history.
